pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

Marta and Jonas Lind keep four rooms on the bank of the river Lisle.

In 2012 Marta and Jonas Lind bought the 1908 mill-keeper's house on the quiet bank of the river Lisle. Two years went into uncovering the original pine floors, freeing the old sash windows and learning the sound of the weir. In 2014 the house opened to its first guests.

They kept only four rooms, so that everyone sits at one long window table for breakfast and the hosts can know each guest by name. Marta bakes and sets the table; Jonas makes the coffee and walks the bank to the weir at 16:00.

pages.title: Rooms
pages.content:
Rooms

Four rooms, breakfast included, €140 to €195 a night.

Willow Room, ground floor, queen bed, 2 guests, 18 m², €140 per night. Loft Room, top floor under the beams, king or twin, 2 guests, 24 m², €150 per night. Weir Room, first floor with a bay window over the weir, king bed, 2 guests, 22 m², €165 per night. Boathouse Room, the small timber boathouse at the water's edge with its own deck, king bed and day bed, up to 3 guests, 28 m², €195 per night.

Rates are for two guests, per night, breakfast included. A third guest in the Boathouse Room is €35 per night. Minimum two nights on Friday and Saturday.

pages.title: Breakfast
pages.content:
Breakfast

At the window table, 08:00 to 10:00.

Ana's sourdough and rye, Lotte's plum, apricot and rhubarb jams, butter and soft cheese from the valley, eggs cooked to order, yoghurt with stewed fruit, coffee by Jonas, tea and fresh juice.

Breakfast is included for every guest. Tell Marta about dietary needs when you ask about dates. A river basket with bread, cheese, fruit and a flask is €22; order it the evening before.

pages.title: The river
pages.content:
The river

The river Lisle runs past the breakfast table.

Every afternoon at 16:00 Jonas walks the bank to the weir, 2.4 km in about forty minutes on a flat path. Anyone staying in the house may come.

Karim Haddad keeps the rowing boats at the mill pond and lends one to guests from May to September, free of charge, with life vests in the boathouse.

pages.title: The stay
pages.content:
The stay

How a stay runs, from the first email to the jar of jam you take home.

Ask: one email or the form on the ask page with dates, room and guests; Marta replies within 24 hours with the deposit link. Arrive: 15:00 to 19:00, tea on the river terrace. Breakfast: 08:00 to 10:00 at the window table. Leave: 11:00, and a jar of the week's jam goes home with you.

Quiet after 22:00, no smoking, children welcome, no pets. Four parking places at the house; the train to Millbrook plus a 12-minute walk. The house rests from 6 to 31 January.

pages.title: Ask about dates
pages.content:
Ask about dates

One way to ask: write to Marta.

Send your dates, the room you would like and the number of guests. Marta confirms within 24 hours and sends a deposit link for 30% of the stay. Cancellation is free up to 14 days before arrival.

Contact

pages.title: The river letter
pages.content:
The river letter

Four letters a year, from the house.

Once a season Marta writes a short letter about the river, the table and the weeks ahead.

posts.title: Ruth and Daniel's three mornings at the window
posts.excerpt: Ruth and Daniel came for their 40th anniversary and moved their chairs to the window every morning.
posts.content:
Ruth and Daniel came to the Weir Room for three nights to mark their fortieth wedding anniversary. They arrived on a Thursday at four, in time for tea on the river terrace, and Jonas walked them along the bank to the weir before the light went.

On the first morning they sat where the table was set for them, with their backs to the room. On the second they asked Marta if they could turn their chairs to face the window, and on the third nobody needed to ask: the two chairs were already there, facing the water, with the board of bread and the jam from Lotte's orchard between them.

Marta sliced Ana's loaf at the kitchen window each morning while they ate. 'We moved our chairs to the window every morning,' Ruth wrote in the visitors' book, and underneath, in Daniel's hand: 'and we would again.' The Weir Room is on the first floor, with a king bed and a bay window over the water.

posts.title: Walking the weir path at four
posts.excerpt: Every afternoon at 16:00 Jonas walks the bank to the weir, 2.4 km in about forty minutes on a flat path.
posts.content:
At four o'clock Jonas puts down the tea towel and walks to the end of the garden, where the path along the bank begins. Anyone staying in the house may come. The walk to the weir is 2.4 km, flat all the way, and takes about forty minutes if nobody stops to look at the heron, which somebody always does.

In autumn the mist lies on the water until well after breakfast and lifts from the far bank first. Jonas knows where the alders lean over the path and where the bank is soft after rain, and he draws the route on the back of a menu for anyone who would rather go alone.

The walk ends at the weir, where the river drops half a metre and makes the sound the house is named after. Most people stand there for a while and then walk back in the lower light, in time for the lamps.

posts.title: Rowing out with Karim
posts.excerpt: From May to September Karim Haddad lends a wooden rowing boat from the mill pond jetty to guests of the house.
posts.content:
Karim Haddad keeps the rowing boats at the mill pond, a ten-minute walk upstream from the house. From May to September he lends one to any guest who asks, free of charge, with a life vest from the boathouse and a short lesson in how not to go in circles.

The Okafor family took a boat out on their second afternoon. The children rowed, badly, and their parents steered, worse, and they came back an hour later with wet sleeves and a handful of watercress that Karim told them was safe to eat.

Ask Marta when you write about dates if you would like a boat on a particular afternoon; Karim likes a day's notice, and the pond is calmest before eleven.
